title: The line pays me. You don't.
subtitle: How advisor compensation actually works, and why your fare is not the thing that changes.

text: Your fare is the same or better. My fee is not added to it.
sub: Cruise lines build the cost of distribution into every fare they publish. It is spent whether an advisor is involved or not. If nobody is, the line simply keeps it.

items.head: The line pays the advisor
items.body: Commission comes out of the fare the line already published. It is not a surcharge sitting on top of your booking.

items.head: Your fare is not marked up
items.body: I cannot inflate a cruise fare. I quote what the line and my consortium make available - often less than retail.

items.head: The services are complimentary
items.body: Planning, cabin selection, watching the fare after you book, answering the phone in a crisis. All of it included.

title: Two ways to hold the booking
Where each part of it sits

points.label: The published fare
points.value: Already contains the cost of distributing it. That cost is spent either way.

points.label: The line
points.value: Pays commission out of that, to whoever holds the booking - or to nobody.

points.label: The traveller
points.value: Pays the fare. Not a penny of my compensation is added on top of it.

points.label: The advisor
points.value: Is paid after you sail, which is a useful thing to know about my incentives.

quote: My advice is candid, my services are complimentary, and every recommendation is one I'd be glad to defend over dinner.

title: Send this to whoever you'd share a cabin with
body: If the fare is the same either way, the only question left is who you'd rather have holding the file when the plan comes apart.
